result.title: Scope-Gap Injection: Exploiting Evaluator Channel Blind Spots in the OpenClaw Agent Security Competition
result.summary: This paper introduces Scope-Gap Injection (SGI), an indirect prompt injection method for multi-stage LLM-agent safety pipelines. In the IJCAI 2026 OpenClaw Agent Security Attack Competition, each attack package is judged by a static skill scan (S1), an LLM-judge safety check over the task and skill definition (S2), and a live execution audit (S3). Our observations suggest a scope gap: S2 appears to inspect the task instruction and skill definition without inspecting attachment contents, while the agent reads attachments during S3. SGI keeps the visible task and skill benign, while target identifiers, bypass parameters, and authorization procedures are moved into an attachment written as a business worklist. The S2 judge therefore sees a harmless task, while the agent follows the hidden worklist and triggers the permission bypass. In OpenClaw, SGI bypassed all three stages for 5 of 19 targets. The highest-scoring single submission achieved $F = 0.385$. Across the submission campaign, attachment placement was associated with higher aggregate S2 acceptance than in-skill placement: 78% versus 23%. We close with defenses that align evaluator scope with the channels available to the agent.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 Scope-Gap Injection 间接提示注入方法，利用多阶段 agent 安全流水线中 LLM judge 只审查任务与技能定义、不读附件内容的通道盲区，把目标标识与绕过参数藏入附件，在 OpenClaw 竞赛的 19 个目标中使 5 个通过全部三阶段检查。
AI.relevance_reason: 「评估者检查的通道与 agent 实际读取的通道不一致」这一设定，可能为核查 LVR 中的视觉旁路、答案是否真正使用 latent 内容以及忠实性评估本身的有效边界提供启发线索。
